topics: reading: Ancient civilizations — Mesopotamia and the birth of writing
written expression: what we owe to ancient civilizations

paper:
Mesopotamia, which means “the land between the rivers”, lay between the Tigris and the Euphrates, mainly in what is now Iraq. Around 3200 BC, the Sumerians, who had settled in the south of this fertile plain, developed one of the first writing systems in the world. They pressed a sharpened reed into soft clay tablets, which left wedge-shaped marks. Historians call this script cuneiform.

At first, writing was used to record goods such as grain and cattle. Later, scribes used it to write letters, stories and laws. Around 1750 BC, the Babylonian king Hammurabi had his famous code of laws carved on a stone pillar. Although the cities of Mesopotamia declined after centuries of wars, their heritage has survived: the 60-minute hour and the 360-degree circle come from their counting system, which was based on 60.

Part One (13 pts)

  1. Write True or False: a) Mesopotamia was located between two rivers. b) Cuneiform signs were written with ink on paper. c) Writing was first used to record goods.
  2. Answer: a) Who developed cuneiform writing? b) What did Hammurabi do around 1750 BC?
  3. What do the underlined words refer to? “They pressed a sharpened reed” ; “their heritage has survived”.
  4. Find in the text words closest in meaning to: a) created ≈ …… ; b) became weaker ≈ ……
  5. Join with after and the past perfect: “The Sumerians settled in the south. Then they developed writing.”
  6. Rewrite starting with the word given: “Although the cities of Mesopotamia declined, their heritage survived.” → Despite ……

Part Two (7 pts)

Write a paragraph of about 80 words explaining what today’s world owes to ancient civilizations (writing, laws, science, architecture…). Use the past simple, the present perfect and linking words.
